title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
statement: On an old phone keypad, digits 2 to 9 carry letters: 2 has abc, 3 has def, and so on up to 9 with wxyz. Given a string of such digits, list every word you could spell by taking one letter for each digit in order. An empty input gives an empty list.

example.caption: Digit 2 offers a, b, c and digit 3 offers d, e, f, so there are 3 x 3 = 9 words.

idea.sentence: Each digit is one level of a tree. At a level, try every letter on that digit, go down to the next digit, then undo the letter to try the next.

jargon.plain: Make a choice, explore everything that follows, then undo the choice and try the next one.
All ways to pick one item from each of several lists. This problem is exactly that, one list per digit.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a string of digits 2 to 9, e.g. 23 (keep it to 2 digits)

compare.bruteLabel: Build the product list by list
compare.unit: words built (rough: 3 to 4 choices per digit, so exponential)

rows.name: Iterative product
rows.note: Start with [''] and for each digit extend every word so far by each letter. Keeps every half-built word alive at once.

rows.name: Backtracking
rows.note: At most 4 letters per digit, so at most 4^n words, each n long. One shared path is built and undone, so only the output is large.

fast.takeaway: Both produce the same words. Backtracking needs only one path in memory at a time, besides the answer.

stages.title: Start empty
stages.note: No digits means no words, so return an empty list. Otherwise path holds one letter per digit so far.

stages.title: Look at a digit
stages.note: Find the letters printed on this digit. Each one will be tried in turn.

stages.title: Pick a letter
stages.note: Push the letter on the path and go to the next digit.

stages.title: Record
stages.note: When every digit has a letter, join the path into a word and save it.

stages.title: Undo
stages.note: Pop the letter and try the next one. Return all words at the end.

edges.title: Empty input
edges.why: No digits means no words. Without the early return, the walk would save one empty word.

edges.title: One digit
edges.why: One level, three letters, three words of length one.

edges.title: Four-letter digits
edges.why: 7 and 9 each carry four letters, so 4 x 4. The branch factor is not always 3.

edges.title: Same digit twice
edges.why: Each level is independent. The same digit twice gives the full 3 x 3 grid, including aa, bb and cc.

gotchas.text: Check digits === '' before the walk and return []. Starting the recursion on an empty string would save [''] (one empty word), which is wrong for this problem.
Digits are characters. Number(digits[i]) - 2 turns '2' into index 0. Using the character directly as an index would read the wrong row or undefined.
path is a []byte, and string(path) copies it. Appending the byte slice itself would alias one backing array and every saved word would change.
Index the letters table with digits[i]-'2'. digits[i] is a byte, so the subtraction gives a small number with no conversion needed.
Digits 7 and 9 have four letters, the others three. Read the letters from a table instead of assuming 3.

recap.key: For digit i, try each of its letters: push, recurse on i + 1, pop. Save the word when i == n. Return [] for empty input.
recap.complexity: Time O(n · 4ⁿ). Space O(n) for the recursion, plus the output.
moves: Look up the letters for digits[i]
Push a letter, recurse on i + 1, pop
At i == n join the path and save the word
